image_description: A male Wood Duck (Aix sponsa) floating on water. The bird displays characteristic colorful plumage with an iridescent green and purple crested head, red eye, white facial markings, a chestnut breast, and tan flanks. It has a distinctive broad, multi-colored bill. The body is partially submerged in rippling blue water.

It is multi-colored with red, black, and white/yellow bands, typical of a Wood Duck. The visible eye is distinctly red with a dark pupil, not uniformly dark as described in the generic prior. This is a species-specific trait of the Wood Duck.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage is indeed colorful and indicative of breeding male status, but the pattern does not match the Mallard (green head/white ring/grey body) or the generic chestnut/grey description.
